subject: Chemistry
solution:
Key idea: Tollens' reagent oxidises only a free –CHO group. A cyclic sugar can give –CHO only if its anomeric carbon is a hemiacetal (free $\mathrm{-OH}$ and ring $\mathrm{O}$ on the same carbon), because the ring then opens to the aldehyde in base.
If the anomeric $\mathrm{-OH}$ is replaced by $\mathrm{-OCH_3}$, the carbon is an acetal (a glycoside). It is stable in base, cannot open, and does not reduce Tollens' reagent.
Structure A: the anomeric carbon has a free $\mathrm{-OH}$. It is a hemiacetal, so it reacts and gives a silver mirror.
Structure D: the anomeric carbon has a free $\mathrm{-OH}$. It is a hemiacetal, so it reacts.
Structure B: the anomeric carbon has $\mathrm{-OCH_3}$ (a methyl glucoside). It is an acetal and does not react.
Structure C: the anomeric carbon of the furanose ring has $\mathrm{-OCH_3}$. It is an acetal and does not react.
Answer: (D) B and C
